The following notes were provided:
Found by wave 14 of an evolutionary beam search (source w14<-e2[swap]):

structured perturbation of known good packings, followed by numerical refinement (sequential linear programming over separating-axis constraints, margin homotopy, clearance ladder). 34 rotated squares; not 180-degree symmetric; not analytically optimised.
The following method summary was provided:

I essentially vibe coded an annealing program and tuned its meta-parameters. Then I fed it known-good packings from previous waves, which made it an evolutionary algorithm, and added constraints such as a fixed number of unrotated squares. Finally I fed it the existing record, with the symmetry assumptions of David Ellsworth's analytic solution relaxed (s = 8.803382739007741), and that worked: after two intermediate packings it produced s = 8.802212238746405, in minutes on my CPU.

The following notes were provided by the submitter:
Found using the same CPU code I use for other polygon packing (on Erich's site).

This packing was found from randomized initial configurations and had zero input from any other records/configurations. I wrote the original implementation myself and have had AI check for bugs (basically as a rubber duck replacement).

The main local solver uses L-BFGS (using a slightly modified LBFGSpp) to optimize each squares x/y/rotation at a fixed container scale S. The objective combines squared overlap penalties based on SAT tests with squared wall protrusion penalties. Analytic gradients are used on the active branches. An outer loop reduces S and reoptimizes. The search also uses a few techniques to escape from local minima (basin hopping, targeted perturbations and ruin and recreate plus others). I do a final polish which includes using a per square coordinate descent among other things.
The last logged result is s=8.79882518426999738. I refined that layout in a separate program.
I was trying to refine the result further before submitting using higher precision. I was able to reach s=8.79879612851587152562627538544 but that is not yet properly verified.
